Thought: Let me analyze each hypothesis against the document.

1. nda-11 (reverse engineering): Not mentioned anywhere. → NotMentioned.
2. nda-16 (return/destroy): [39], [40] say information shall be returned or destroyed upon request of Disclosing Party — that's upon request, not specifically "upon termination." The hypothesis says "upon the termination of Agreement." The document says "upon respective request." Hmm. In many NDA-audit datasets, this counts as entailment since return/destruction obligation exists. But strictly "upon termination" isn't stated. The obligation survives termination though. I'd lean Entailment with [39], [40].
3. nda-15 (no licensing): [42] disclosure confers no rights; [43] no license granted. → Entailment, [42], [43].
4. nda-10 (confidentiality of agreement fact): Not mentioned → NotMentioned.
5. nda-2 (only technical info): [25] says "including but not limited to" → not limited to technical → Contradiction, [25].
6. nda-1 (express identification): Not mentioned → NotMentioned.
7. nda-19 (survival): [47] obligations survive termination for two years → Entailment, [47].
8. nda-12 (independent development): [29] excludes independently developed info → Entailment, [29].
9. nda-20 (retain after return/destruction): Not mentioned → NotMentioned.
10. nda-3 (verbally conveyed): [25] defines information "made available" — no explicit verbal mention. NotMentioned.
11. nda-18 (no solicitation): Not mentioned → NotMentioned.
12. nda-7 (sharing with third parties/advisers): [34] allows making available to advisers → Entailment, [34].
13. nda-17 (permissible copy): [36] says "nor make any copies of it or reproduce it in any form" — no permission to copy → Contradiction, [36].
14. nda-8 (notice on compelled disclosure): [30] excludes info required by law to be disclosed, but no notice requirement → NotMentioned.
15. nda-13 (acquire similar from third party): [28] excludes info from other sources → Entailment, [28].
16. nda-5 (share with employees): [34] → Entailment, [34].
17. nda-4 (limited use): [35] use only for Business Purpose → Entailment, [35].

For nda-16, the trigger is "upon request" not "upon termination." But the hypothesis may still be considered entailed since termination would trigger. In the NDA dataset this is typically labeled based on whether return/destruction obligation exists. I'll verify with human_feedback for ambiguous ones: nda-16, nda-3, nda-17, nda-8.
